fixes.reason: In afex's aov_car the lme4-style term (Status*Type|SNO) and the explicit Error(SNO/(Status*Type)) are documented equivalent specifications of the same mixed-design model: SNO is the subject identifier and Status*Type the within-subjects part, producing identical ANOVA tables, error strata, and df. The rewrite is purely syntactic and leaves the estimated model unchanged.

fixes.description: anova() called with correction = 'none' for both ANOVA models
fixes.fix: anova() called with correction = 'none' for both ANOVA models
fixes.reason: Sphericity handling for the three-level cue-status factor is an explicitly open ambiguity with stated options (uncorrected df, Greenhouse-Geisser, Huynh-Feldt). Setting correction='none' resolves that ambiguity by selecting the uncorrected option, which changes the error degrees of freedom and hence the p-values (and any df-dependent reporting) for within-subjects effects in both ANOVAs, even though the F numerators are unchanged. It is a described option, not a workaround, so it is major rather than critical.

fixes.reason: The tightened pattern with anchor and length check extracts exactly the rumination-group coefficients that operationalise the paper's stated single-degree-of-freedom interaction comparisons on the contrast scores, and errors loudly otherwise. It does not settle any stated ambiguity (own vs pooled error term, counterbalancing retained or dropped, within-group vs full-model simple effect) and does not alter estimates, sample, or error terms; it is a defensive implementation fix.

No analytical choice (estimator, error term, inclusion of CB) is altered — only how the existing test is extracted.

fixes.fix: After the first clean run, c011 and c012 were both exactly 100%. Inspection showed the sibling-count columns are 1-based codes (min 1, no zeros). Added the 'subtract 1' recoding for Bio_Sib, Half_Sib and Step_Sib and re-ran.

fixes.reason: This is a data-decoding correction, not a change in the estimand. The claims concern the percentage of participants with at least one half-/stepsibling, and the raw columns were found to hold 1-based codes (minimum 1, no zeros), so that 'no siblings' was coded as 1. Subtracting 1 converts the codes back to true sibling counts, preserving the underlying quantities the methods describe (analogous to a value-preserving type coercion / coding-scheme fix). The analysis itself - thresholding counts at >=1 and computing percentages - is unchanged; the fix merely makes the computed percentages match the intended quantity instead of the obviously erroneous 100% for every sibling type, a conclusion supported by direct inspection of the code distribution (min 1, no zeros, implausible 100% on two independent variables). No analytical choice among the plan's stated options was altered, no observations were added or dropped, and no results were fabricated.

quantity.description: Cohen's d = 2.20 for the difference in intimacy between the attention and no attention conditions.

added_choices: The identity of the excluded participant: ID 20. The methods state that one participant was excluded for suspecting the deceptive procedure, but the data file has 30 records and no suspicion variable, so which record to drop is not recoverable from the data. It is recovered here from the paper's own reporting: of the 30 single-record drops, 5 reproduce the methods' sample description (10 males, 19 females, Mage +/- SD = 19.3 +/- 0.89), of which IDs 14 and 20 reproduce all seven a20 quantities, and only ID 20 also reproduces the other Study 2a statistics (friendship t27 = 1.04, p = .306; r27 = .38, p = .045).
Cohen's d from the pooled SD with no small-sample correction (the d formula is not stated).
Student t with pooled variance rather than the Welch correction (not stated; with n = 15 vs 14 the two differ only in the third decimal, and only the pooled version gives the reported df of 27).
Intimacy as the mean of the four items rather than their sum (not stated; the sum is ruled out by the reported means of 4.58 and 2.82 on a seven-point scale).
targeted.notes: The whole gap is the one exclusion the methods state. The closest analyst applied every other choice as the paper made it - item-mean intimacy that matches the workbook's own aggregate, pooled-variance Student t, pooled-SD d - but analysed all 30 records because the data file gives no way to find the excluded case, which yields t(28) = 6.20 and d = 2.26. Dropping the right record moves every one of the seven quantities onto the reported value at once, including the reported df of 27; the attention condition's mean and SD are already exact on the full 30 records, which places the excluded participant in the no attention condition. Attempt 4 (Hedges-corrected d on all 30 records) also lands on d = 2.20, but it is a coincidence: it leaves t, df and the no attention mean and SD wrong, so it is not the route. Two records, ID 14 and ID 20, are interchangeable for this analysis - both give identical a20 values - and ID 20 is picked because it also fits the study's other reported statistics. Every choice used is either stated in the methods or listed as open in the contract; the only thing added is which record the stated exclusion removes.
targeted.diagnosis:
*Unblinded conjecture — I have seen the reported values; this grades nothing.*

The blind analysts and the paper differ on exactly one thing: sample size. Everything else the analysts chose was right.

`closest_replica.R` got every open choice the way the paper made it. Intimacy as the item mean of r1, r6, r7 and the reverse-coded 8 − r4 is confirmed by the workbook's own precomputed "Intimacy" column, which the script checks to 1e-10. The pooled-variance Student t, the two-tailed p, and Cohen's d from the pooled SD all match. My attempts 2 and 3 confirm the alternatives are dead ends: Welch leaves d untouched and gives df = 27.92, and summing the items puts the means at 18.3 and 11.3 against reported 4.58 and 2.82.

The script also states the problem plainly in its own comments: the paper reports 29 after excluding one suspicious participant, the file has 30 records, and no suspicion variable exists. The analyst analysed all 30 and flagged the discrepancy. That is the correct blind decision, and it is the entire source of the gap.

The signature that this is the whole story: on all 30 records the attention condition already reproduces 4.58 and .82 exactly. Only the no-attention side is off. The excluded participant is therefore in the no-attention condition, which is also what the paper's own one-sample tests say — t<sub>13</sub> against t<sub>14</sub>.

So this is not analytical divergence. It is an unrecoverable exclusion. The suspicion flag existed on the authors' side and never made it into the shared file. Any blind analyst would land on d = 2.26 and be unable to do better, because the information needed to pick the right record is not in the data — I recovered it only by reading the paper's results back into the search.
